item.title: What Your Make-Do Workspace Is Doing To Your Health: Hidden Cost For Women
item.description: Women often operate in temporary, shared, or improvised workspaces in many homes and offices. A chair for eating becomes a chair for working. A laptop is on a low table or a bed. Throughout the day, work moves from the desk to the sofa to the kitchen counter. Most people agree that this culture of adjustment is useful. People don't talk about the physical cost very often. item.title: Who Is Nithya Raman? Indian-Origin Los Angeles Leader Running For Mayor
item.description: Nithya Raman, an Indian-origin leader, announced her candidacy for mayor of Los Angeles, California, in 2026, challenging incumbent Karen Bass. She aims to address matters like housing, homelessness, government accountability, and public safety. While Raman and Bass have a long history of being cooperative, this election highlights some of the policy gaps and bolder governance needed. item.title: Meet Thanya Nathan, Kerala’s First Civil Judge With Visual Impairment
item.description: Kerala’s judiciary has marked a historic first with a woman with visual impairment qualifying for the Kerala Judicial Service and preparing to assume office as a Civil Judge (Junior Division). Thanya Nathan C, a native of Kannur, topped the merit list under the benchmark disabilities category in the Kerala Judicial Service Examination 2025. item.title: Eight Months Pregnant & A Champion: Rifle Shooter Meghana Sajjanar
item.description: Rifle shooter Meghana Sajjanar won a Bronze medal in the women's 10m rifle event at the Asian Shooting Championship in New Delhi. But her win is not just about standing on the podium; it is about making a statement of courage, discipline, and determination, as she achieved this eight months into her pregnancy. item.title: Meet Anastasiia Gubanova, Georgian Ice Skater Goes Indian At Winter Olympics
item.description: Figure skater Anastasiia Gubanova, representing Georgia, delighted Indian audiences as she performed to Indian songs at the ongoing Winter Olympics 2026 in Milan. In one of the most talked-about moments of the Games, Gubanova performed to trendy Bollywood numbers such as San Sanana from the 2001 film Asoka and the title track of the recent hit Dhurandhar. item.title: Why Side Hustles Feel Mandatory Today: Gen Z Reflects
item.description: For many, pursuing one job does not feel enough. We now see side hustles as a "have to do" thing. People are constantly trying to overburden themselves just to feel that they are doing 'enough'. This shift is changing the whole socio-economic diaspora. Working more feels okay, but doing it without drawing boundaries poses serious threats towards the upcoming generation. item.title: Menopause: Your Body May Be Signalling Mineral Deficiencies
item.description: Many women in perimenopause and menopause describe a deep, persistent tiredness, the kind that doesn’t lift with sleep or time off. item.title: Delhi Missing Persons Panic Fueled Via Paid Promotions? What Police Say
item.description: Social media was flooded this week with unverified posts claiming a sudden spike in missing persons cases in Delhi, triggering widespread concern.
